source.title: Regularity Properties of Sectorial Operators: Counterexamples and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let A be an R-sectorial operator on an L^p-space with p in (1, infinity). Must the sectorial angle omega(A) equal the R-sectorial angle omega_R(A)? The same question is asked under stronger semigroup assumptions: if -A generates an analytic C_0-semigroup, does the equality still hold when the semigroup is positive, contractive, or both positive and contractive?
accepted.context_brief: Angles of R-sectorial operators on L^p

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Let A be an R-sectorial operator on Lp for p ∈ (1, ∞). Does one have ω(A) = ωR(A) (if A generates a positive / contractive / positive contractive analytic C0-semigroup)?
By definition one has ω(A) ≤ ωR(A).
Definition 2.5 (R-Sectorial Operator). A sectorial operator on a Banach space X is called R-sectorial if for some ω ∈ (ω(A), π) one has R{λR(λ, A) : λ 6∈ Σω} < ∞.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a sectorial operator on a UMD-Banach lattice, and assume that -A generates a positive contractive C_0-semigroup. Must A then have a bounded H-infinity calculus, have bounded imaginary powers, or be R-analytic?
accepted.context_brief: Positive contractive semigroups on UMD-Banach lattices

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Let A be a sectorial operator on some UMD-Banach lattice and suppose that −A is the generator of a positive contractive C0-semigroup. Does A have a bounded H∞-calculus (bounded imaginary powers / is R-analytic)?
Definition 2.7 (Bounded H∞-calculus). A sectorial operator A is said to have a bounded H∞(Σσ)-calculus for some σ ∈ (ω(A), π) if the homomorphism f 7→ f(A) from H∞0 (Σσ) to B(X) is bounded.

Definition 2.12 (Bounded Imaginary Powers (BIP)). A sectorial operator on a Banach space X is said to have bounded imaginary powers (BIP) if for all t ∈ R the operator Ait associated to the functions λ 7→ λit via the holomorphic functional calculus is bounded.

accepted.question_text: Find an analogue, in the borderline case omega_H-infinity(A) = pi/2, of the characterizations known below the critical angle. On Hilbert spaces, if -A generates a contractive analytic C_0-semigroup then A has a bounded H-infinity calculus with omega_H-infinity(A) = omega(A) < pi/2, and conversely operators with bounded H-infinity calculus of angle less than pi/2 are similar to generators of contractive analytic semigroups. On L^p-spaces, if -A generates a contractive positive analytic C_0-semigroup then A has a bounded H-infinity calculus with angle less than pi/2, and conversely such operators admit the structural model described in Theorem 2.11. What is the correct corresponding characterization when the H-infinity angle is exactly pi/2?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a similar characterization as in Theorem 2.10 or Theorem 2.11 in the case ωH∞(A) = π/2.
Theorem 2.10. Let A be a sectorial operator on a Hilbert space such that −A generates a contractive analytic C0-semigroup. Then A has a bounded H∞-calculus with ωH∞(A) = ω(A) < π/2.

Theorem 2.11. Let p ∈ (1, ∞) and A be a sectorial operator on an Lp-space Lp(Ω) such that −A generates a contractive positive analytic C0-semigroup. Then A has a bounded H∞-calculus with ωH∞(A) = ωR(A) < π/2.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which C_0-semigroups on L^p-spaces admit a loose dilation within the class of all L^p-spaces. Here a semigroup (T(t))_{t >= 0} has a loose dilation in a class X if there exist a space Y in X, bounded linear maps J: X -> Y and Q: Y -> X, and a bounded C_0-group (U(t))_{t in R} on Y such that T(t) = Q U(t) J for every t >= 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Characterize those semigroups on Lp which have a loose dilation in the class of all Lp-spaces.
(ii) (T(t))t≥0 has a loose dilation in X if for some Y in X there are bounded linear operators J : X → Y and Q: Y → X and a bounded C0-group (U(t))t∈R on Y such that T(t) = QU(t)J for all t ≥ 0.

accepted.question_text: Does every C_0-semigroup of positive contractions on a UMD-Banach lattice admit either a strict dilation or a loose dilation in the class of all UMD-spaces?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Does every C0-semigroup of positive contractions on a UMD-Banach lattice have a strict / loose dilation in the class of all UMD-spaces?

(i) (T(t))t≥0 has a strict dilation in X if for some Y in X there are contractive linear operators J : X → Y and Q: Y → X and an isometric C0-group (U(t))t∈R on Y such that T(t) = QU(t)J for all t ≥ 0.
(ii) (T(t))t≥0 has a loose dilation in X if for some Y in X there are bounded linear operators J : X → Y and Q: Y → X and a bounded C0-group (U(t))t∈R on Y such that T(t) = QU(t)J for all t ≥ 0.

accepted.question_text: Theorem 3.19 states that if a Banach space X admits an unconditional basis, then every negative generator of an analytic semigroup on X is R-sectorial if and only if X is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Does the same equivalence remain true in either of the larger classes consisting of all Banach spaces that admit a Schauder basis, or all separable Banach spaces?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.19. Let X be a Banach space that admits an unconditional basis. Then every negative generator of an analytic semigroup is R-sectorial if and only if X is isomorphic to a Hilbert space.
Problem 8. Does Theorem 3.19 hold in the bigger class of all Banach spaces admitting a Schauder basis / of all separable Banach spaces?
